label: 2026 Orbital Launches
delta: ~105 Falcon-family launches in 2026 as of Sep 6: Starlink 15-24 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1088 19th flight, 27 satellites, 1426 UTC) — SpaceX's 103rd Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the year's 80th dedicated Starlink mission (tallies for the Falcon-family total, which also counts Falcon Heavy flights, vary slightly by source). No launches occurred Sep 3-5. Previously: 104 Falcon-family launches as of Sep 2: Starlink 15-23 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1063 35th flight, 27 V2-Mini satellites, 0842 UTC), the year's 79th Starlink mission. That followed the Aug 30 Falcon Heavy launch of NASA's Roman Space Telescope from LC-39A Kennedy — SpaceX's 102nd Falcon-family orbital launch of 2026 (tallies vary slightly by source) and the sixth NASA flagship-class payload to fly on a Falcon rocket. Previously: 101 launches as of Aug 26 (Starlink 15-22, SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1082 24th flight). The prior launch, Starlink 10-49 (SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1067 37th flight — a new reuse record, 0933 UTC Aug 25), was widely reported as SpaceX's 100th Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and was also the company's last planned Falcon 9 Starlink mission from Florida — SpaceX VP of Launch Kiko Dontchev confirmed Florida Starlink deployment now shifts to Starship, with Vandenberg absorbing the bulk of 2026's remaining Starlink cadence. Roughly 75% of 2026's missions have been Starlink. President Gwynne Shotwell projects ~140-145 Falcon 9 launches for the full year (2024: 138 total missions; 2025: 167). Starship IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) remains pending; an Aug 31 FCC filing set a Sept 15, 2026 target for the flight, SpaceX's first attempt at reaching full orbital velocity, with roughly 20 operational Starlink V3 satellites on the manifest.

label: Total Booster Recoveries (All-Time)
delta: 659th: OCISLY droneship touchdown (223rd on that vessel) after Starlink 15-24 from Vandenberg (B1088, 19th flight), Sep 6. 658th: OCISLY droneship touchdown after Starlink 15-23 from Vandenberg (B1063, 35th flight), Sep 2. 656th-657th: Falcon Heavy's two side boosters landed simultaneously at Cape Canaveral on the Aug 30 Roman Space Telescope launch — Landing Zone 2 (19th landing on that pad) and Landing Zone 40 (6th) — the center core was expended for extra performance to the Sun-Earth L2 transfer. 655th: OCISLY droneship touchdown (221st on that vessel) after Starlink 15-22 from Vandenberg (B1082, 24th flight), Aug 26. 654th: ASOG droneship touchdown (165th on that vessel) after Starlink 10-49 from Cape Canaveral (B1067, 37th flight — a new single-booster reuse record), Aug 25 — SpaceX's last planned Falcon 9 Starlink landing tied to a Florida launch. Two landings Aug 21: OCISLY (220th on vessel) after Starlink 15-20 from Vandenberg (B1100, 9th flight), and ASOG (164th on vessel) after Starlink 10-39 from Cape Canaveral (B1078, 30th flight). 651st: OCISLY landing after the Aug 19 Starlink Group 17-50 mission from Vandenberg (B1097, 12th flight). 650th: OCISLY landing after the Aug 15 USSF-366 mission from Vandenberg (B1088, 18th flight) — the second half of a record 38.5-minute dual-launch turnaround. 649th (same day): Landing Zone 40 touchdown after the Aug 15 Globalstar 2-R mission from Cape Canaveral (B1090, 14th flight). Note: IFT-12 Booster 19 (May 22) and IFT-13 Booster 20 (July 24) were NOT recovered — both lost during off-nominal landing-burn/splashdown attempts in Gulf of Mexico ocean landings (Starship boosters are not counted in this Falcon-family recovery tally).

label: Starlink Satellites in Orbit
delta: ~11,093 in orbit / ~11,078 operational as of Sep 6, 2026, per Jonathan McDowell's tracking (12,881 launched all-time), reflecting the Sep 2 and Sep 6 Starlink deployments (27 satellites each, Vandenberg) net of ongoing deorbits of older units. Previously: ~11,093 in orbit / ~11,078 working as of Sep 3, 2026. Earlier: ~11,102 in orbit per McDowell as of Aug 27; ~11,050 as of Aug 26 following the Aug 25 Starlink 10-49 (29 sats) and Aug 26 Starlink 15-22 (27 sats) launches — the latter the first Starlink deployment since SpaceX ended Falcon 9 Starlink launches from Florida. SpaceX filed an FCC application July 6 for up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites across two new VLEO shells with W-/D-band frequencies, positioned as AI-data-center backhaul infrastructure in addition to consumer broadband. Aug 4 Q2 earnings: Starlink generated $4.3B of SpaceX's $7.81B quarterly revenue (55% of total).

label: Max Single Booster Reflights
delta: B1067 set a new record with its 37th flight on the Starlink 10-49 mission (Aug 25, 2026, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral) — also SpaceX's last planned Falcon 9 Starlink launch from Florida. Previously: 36th flight on Starlink 10-42 (July 9, 2026) — the first orbital booster in history to reach 36 flights; 34th flight on Starlink 10-44 (Mar 30, 2026).

label: Starship Integrated Flight Tests
delta: IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) update: as of Sept 7, both vehicles have finished their required single-vehicle tests and are in final checkout — Ship 41 in Mega Bay 2, Booster 21 in Mega Bay 1, with Flight Termination System placards now visible on both bays. Next steps are loading the Starlink V3 payload into Ship 41, then rolling the booster and ship out for stacking; the current no-earlier-than date is still Sept 15, 2026, per CADENA/COMPASS Space Operations planning slides, though SpaceX has not made that an official target. An Aug 31 FCC filing requesting Starlink V3 spectrum authorization set Sept 15 as the target launch/deployment date — the first filing to put a full orbital-insertion profile on Flight 14's paperwork, confirming Musk's Aug 4 earnings-call comment that the flight would carry next-generation V3 satellites (~20 units, ~1 Tbps downlink each) into an operational orbit rather than the short suborbital arcs flown since IFT-6. On Sept 3-4, the FAA issued a Finding of No Significant Impact on its Final Tiered Environmental Assessment for expanded Starship reentry/landing options — a new Northern Pacific contingency area plus expanded Hawaii/Central Pacific and Southeast Pacific contingency zones — giving SpaceX backup splashdown options if the Boca Chica return path or catch tower can't be used; the primary recovery plan for Ship 41 remains an Indian Ocean splashdown, per Musk's Aug 20 comment that a tower catch of the ship is still 'a few months' out rather than on Flight 14. Separately, next-generation Ship 42 rolled out to Massey's Test Site and completed a pair of cryogenic proof tests (methane and LOX header tanks) late Sept 3, clearing it to return to Mega Bay 2 for engine installation ahead of a later flight. Hardware status leading into checkout: Booster 21 completed a full 33-engine static fire at Pad 2 Aug 28, and underwent a chopsticks lift-and-catch rehearsal on the launch tower Aug 29; Ship 41 completed single-engine (Aug 19) and six-engine (Aug 21) static fires at Massey's Test Site. IFT-13 (Booster 20 V3 + Ship 40 V3) completed July 24, 2026 after a July 16 T-0 abort (6 Raptors flagged low LOX turbopump pressure from moisture; 2 engines replaced before reflight). Results: first-ever deployment of operational satellites — 20 V3 Starlink sats (6 with cameras) released in suborbit and contacted ground stations; Ship 40 relit all 3 Raptors and made a soft Indian Ocean splashdown, remaining intact afterward for the first close-up post-flight heat-shield inspection. Booster 20 was lost on its Gulf of Mexico splashdown attempt — only 10 of 13 landing-burn engines relit, 5 shut down seconds later, causing a hard impact. Prior: FAA cleared Starship to resume flights July 13, 2026, closing the IFT-12 mishap investigation (heat effects on propulsion + erroneous engine alarm settings that prevented Booster 19's reignition, May 22 loss).

label: SPCX (Nasdaq) — Post-IPO Trading
source: SEC EDGAR S-1 / CNBC / Bloomberg / Nasdaq / StockAnalysis.com
contestNote: Fell more than 4% on Sep 9, 2026 to ~$148.32 (from Sep 8's close of $153.47) as the Day-90 lock-up tranche — roughly 319M restricted shares (~$49B at the prior close) — became eligible to trade, erasing the prior session's gain. The move closely mirrored the ~4% drop seen on the similarly sized Aug 20 unlock (which rebounded within a session), and contrasted with the much larger Aug 6 unlock (911.5M shares), after which SPCX rose 6.1%. A further ~59.1M affiliate shares unlock Sep 10, with a much larger ~328M-share tranche tied to November earnings. Analyst Jeffrey Wlodarczak (Pivotal Research) initiated coverage with a Buy rating and $220 target, saying SpaceX's valuation hinges on making Starship rapidly reusable; the broader analyst set (33 covering, per TipRanks) rates it a Moderate Buy with an average target of ~$231 (range $212-$280), implying substantial upside from current levels once unlock-driven supply is absorbed. Previously: closed at $149.74 on Sep 4 and traded $147.32-$150.85 on Sep 6 (last quote $147.95, down 1.2% intraday) — up roughly 19% over the trailing 4 weeks — as the market looked ahead to the Sep 9 unlock and Starship Flight 14's Sep 15 target date. Earlier: closed at $141.50 on Aug 28, 2026 (per Motley Fool). Bears (Motley Fool, Investing.com) argue the staggered unlocks could 'swamp retail investors' given SpaceX 'isn't particularly close to recurring profits.' Aug 24 also brought Musk's confirmation that SpaceX and Nvidia designed a Vera Rubin NVL72 compute system for 'Starmind AI1,' SpaceX's first orbital AI data-center satellite, targeting a Q4 2027 launch — a year earlier than the 2028-earliest timeline SpaceX gave investors in its May 2026 S-1. That announcement landed the day before SpaceX and Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry announced a $100B 'Starbase Louisiana' spaceport in Vermilion Parish — the same day SpaceX flew its last planned Falcon 9 Starlink launch from Florida (Starlink 10-49, booster B1067's record 37th flight). Earlier: SPCX fell 3.88% on Aug 14 as the $60B all-stock closing of the Anysphere (Cursor) acquisition added ~391M new Class A shares to a market already digesting post-lockup supply; that interrupted a rally from a 52-week low of $104.83 (Aug 3) to $146.15 intraday (Aug 13), driven by a filing showing Musk's 48.4% stake worth over $900B. Aug 6 lock-up expiration released up to 911.5M insider shares (~$100B) without triggering a sell-off (+6.1%); shares jumped 15.8% Aug 7-8 on the Q2 earnings beat and the $16.8B Terafab chip-plant confirmation. IPO recap: priced at $135/share June 11 (largest IPO in history, $1.77T implied valuation); all-time high $225.64 June 16; joined Nasdaq-100 July 7. Musk holds ~42-48% economic equity (filings vary by measurement date and post-Cursor dilution), ~79-85% voting control (dual-class Class B) — cannot be removed as director except by his own vote.
